messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The “largest” planet we’ve ever seen is still a matter of definition, but the biggest **confirmed** planet (not a brown dwarf) that astronomers have measured is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**.

| Property | HD 100546 b | Jupiter (for comparison) |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------|
| Mass | ≈ 20 M_J (≈ 0.02 M_⊙) | 1 M_J |
| Radius | ≈ 2.5 R_J | 1 R_J |
| Orbital distance | ~10 AU from its star | 5.2 AU (Saturn) |
| Age | ~5 Myr (still forming) | – |

Because it’s still accreting material, its radius is inflated, and it sits right on the boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs. If you include objects that are technically brown dwarfs (objects that fuse deuterium), the size limit goes up to about 2–3 R_J, but those are usually classified as substellar objects rather than planets.

So, in short: **HD 100546 b** is the largest planet we’ve actually measured. Beyond that, we’re still discovering more massive exoplanets and brown dwarfs, so the “largest planet in the universe” could change as new data come in.
